newsitem.title: UK: Stocks fall in Asia, Europe.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall in Asia, Europe.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Tuesday.

LONDON - Stocks finished moderately lower as investors remained nervous about a possible Wall Street slide after its recent weakness. Although the Dow has dropped 5 percent since hitting an all-time peak last month, many market participants believe U.S. blue chips are due for a more substantial correction. The FTSE 100 index ended 14.2 points down at 3,979.6.

FRANKFURT - Stocks reversed most of the gains made the previous day as the overnight retreat of the dollar and weakness on Wall Street dampened sentiment. The DAX-30 index of 30 top German shares closed 40.66 points lower at 2,815.13. The IBIS DAX, measuring all-day electronic dealings in the DAX, later ended at 2,808.50 points.

PARIS - Shares closed 1.3 percent lower on the weakness in Wall Street and higher than expected U.S. November housing starts, and despite a slight cut in interest rates by the Bank of France. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 28.87 points at 2,193.70.

ZURICH - Shares closed lower in sagging volume and nervous trade as investors concentrated on U.S. approval for Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz to merge as Novartis, the world's second biggest pharmaceuticals company. The All-share SPI closed down 11.82 points, or 0.48 percent, to 2,459.92.

TOKYO - Stocks ended mixed in narrow range trade, with the key stock index closing marginally lower. Early losses were mostly offset by fresh buying and short-covering in sectors that had been hammered recently, such as construction and banking. The key 225-issue Nikkei average finished 8.58 points or 0.04 percent lower at 20,413.46.

HONG KONG - Stocks closed down, with the upcoming U.S. central bank policy meeting on interest rates providing the reason to take some gains. The Hang Seng Index closed down 122.11 points at 12,815.37, after bouncing off a low of 12,747.91.
SYDNEY - Shares ambled to a lower close after a drop in the Dow depressed sentiment and a crumbling copper price impacted on BHP. The All Ordinaries index fell 20.5 points to 2,315.8.

JOHANNESBURG - Stocks had a rollercoaster day, battered by as a whirlwind of selling from the futures market. Early trade pushed industrial shares briefly higher but waves of selling later thrust the market down. The all-share index ended the day down 98.5 points at 6,384.0 and industrials tumbled 113.6 points to 7,568.9. The gold index shed 33.9 points to end at 1,477.7.
